ownedBy: town-canon-reviewer (see .claude/agents/town-canon-reviewer.md — Pass 1 canon, Pass 2 realism, Pass 3 anti-cliché)
purpose: Machine-readable town criteria, authored from the 2026-08-29 Millcross tent-removal review (docs/worldbuilding/reviews/2026-08-29-millcross-tent-removal-and-criteria.md). Three consumers, all data-driven: (1) a future consistency test asserts plan files against `measured` + `towns.*.ratified`; (2) tools/art-forge/generate/prompt-lint.mjs merges `antiCliche.forbiddenVocabulary` into its token data (R2-style) and `towns.*.briefs.countBand` into its R4 count checks; (3) tools/art-forge/forge.config.json styleGuard merges the same vocabulary at generation time. Nothing in this file is prompt text; everything is lint/check data.
honestyRule: Every rule carries `source`. Values tagged `canon:` or `measured:` cite their file and section; values tagged `owner-decision:` cite the date and the decision; values tagged `reviewer:` are authored by the town-canon-reviewer in this file and claim NO canon force — an INVENTED value claiming canon force is a VETO under the role's veto policy. Amend canon in canon files (A0/A1/A3, style.md), never here.

realism.value: every asserted building material must be producible by the town's stated economy and transport, or shippable by its own traffic (here: river + cart). Millcross local set: mill timber → frames; river stone → footings; valley clay/lime → whitewashed plaster; slate → steep roofs; fired brick → chimney stacks, plinths, garden-wall courses — slate and brick shipped in as barge ballast on the river trade and landed at the ford; canvas only as the temporary road-side camp register
realism.source: reviewer:REVIEWER, grounded in canon:A1 amended material sentence — Pass 2 asks 'who ships shingle to a river-ford town?' and the amended §6 answers it (the timber rows are the mill's output); amended 2026-09-01, owner option b, verdicts #12–#14 (slate + fired brick arrive as barge ballast, landed at the ford)
realism.check: consistency test cross-references each brief material against the town's materials-by-economy list

realism.value: timber frames on stone footings with plastered walls is STRUCTURE (canon); decorative storybook fachwerk patterns, gingerbread trim and exposed ornamental bracing are a forbidden REGISTER
realism.source: reviewer:REVIEWER — separates the structural fact the owner ratified from the cliché the owner rejected (realistic-but-fantasy, not cliché)
realism.check: prompt may contain 'timber-framed', 'plastered'; may not contain the antiCliche decoration vocabulary

realism.value: steep pitched roofs (shingle or slate) suit a river-valley rain/snow load; flag flat or tiled-roof clichés that carry no local warrant
realism.check: brief roof words resolve to the town's material list

realism.value: each town's silhouette is singular and non-transferable: Millcross = one horizontal low ribbon + one tall mill housing + chimney stacks; Embervale's forty smoke plumes and Norhollow's palisade line belong to those towns and must not migrate into a Millcross brief
realism.check: brief mustNotShow borrows the other towns' silhouette tokens (palisade, forty-smoke)

forbiddenVocabulary.appliesTo: town brief positive prompts (merged into prompt-lint R2 data and styleGuard at generation time; union with forge.config.json forbiddenTokens — do not duplicate that modern-contamination list here)
forbiddenVocabulary.source: reviewer:REVIEWER (Pass 3, v1.1), each token grounded: storybook/quaint/gingerbread/fachwerk = storybook half-timbered-everything register; cobblestone = era law says hard-packed earth roads (ERA) + A1; windmill = canon water mill (ABP mustNotShow); castle/citadel/keep = the fortress register — a TOWN wall is legal since 2026-08-29 evening (rampart/palisade removed from this list then, they are wall synonyms the walled brief may need), a CASTLE never is; lanterns/glow/tavern sign/bunting = generic-fantasy defaults that erase the 'cheap light' register; fantasy/medieval village = the generic label that pastes over the specific town
forbiddenVocabulary.note: a cliché is a RECOMMENDATION unless it breaks a style law; these tokens are style-law breaks (era, palette, wall-less canon) or the owner's explicit not-cliché direction, which is why they are lint data and not advice
forbiddenVocabulary.check: prompt-lint R2 throws when any token appears in a composed positive prompt

allowedCharacteristics: painted-realistic finish over readable large shapes
legible silhouette grammar (one dominant mass, clear secondary rhythm)
warm civic solidity — a place people maintain, not a ruin or a camp
a real approach road that composes the frame
forbiddenCharacteristics: castle-scale towers, citadel keeps and fantasy-brochure battlements (Millcross is a working town wall, not a fortress)
storybook pastels and glow (palette is ash-grey/rope-brown/tallow, cheap light)
clean fantasy-brochure weathering (era law: unpainted wood, mud, wear)
church spires, belfry towers and cupola halls (no church is ratified in Millcross's venue list; A1 §6: nothing else competes with the mill housing)
roof pinnacles and finials (ornament classes adjacent to the banned battlements)

crenellations, battlements and machicolations on non-military structures (verdict #15 rail, owner-approved 2026-09-01: the class, not just the scale — a crenellated town tower is still fortress register)

referencePolicy.source: owner-decision:OWNER-2026-08-29 (named as characteristics only, never as prompt text) + REVIEWER split of allowed vs forbidden characteristics; crenellation class extended 2026-09-01, owner-approved, verdict #15 rail
referencePolicy.check: no proper noun from the references may appear in a prompt (prompt-lint R2 data); renders are reviewed against the allowed/forbidden characteristic lists, not token-matched
